the fractal dimension D of a Potts cluster is equal to the critical exponent of its mass m.
the corrections to scaling are of the form: M ( L ) = L ^{D} [ 1 + A _{1} ln L + A _{2} ( ln L ) ^{2} +... ], where D is the exact asymptotic exponent and A _{1}, A _{2},... are constants.

the fractal dimensions and corrections to scaling for the Fortuin-Kastelyn cluster hull, external perimeter and singly connected bonds are exactly known for all q-state Potts critical models in 2 dimensions, and that the total mass of the cluster is exactly known for q = 2, 4, and 6.

the study of the scaling properties of the Potts models at their critical points, in particular, the fractal dimensions of critical clusters, the corrections to scaling and the fractal dimensions and corrections to scaling of critical percolation clusters in the q → 1 limit of the Potts model.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the asymptotic mass of the hull, singly connected bonds, external perimeter and total mass are all given by the same exponent, but with different logarithmic corrections, and with a different leading term for the singly connected bonds.
the asymptotic fractal dimensions of the hull, singly connected bonds, external perimeter and total mass of critical FK clusters are, for all q, equal to 1/2, 1, 1, and 1/2 respectively.

the asymptotics of the fractal masses of critical Potts clusters is not a simple power law, and that the corrections to the power laws, when they exist, are not always logarithmic, but may be of the type log-log, log-sqrt-log, or even log-log-log-log.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found that the corrections to the scaling exponents for the hull and singly connected bonds are of the form 1/n^2, and that there are logarithmic corrections to the scaling of the external perimeter and the total mass.
, for q = 2, the corrections to scaling are of the same form as for the Ising model, whereas, for q =4, there is a new, logarithmic, contribution to the correction to scaling.
the corrections are of the order of (ln N)^2, where N is the number of sites in the cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fractal dimensions are universal in the sense that they do not depend on q.
, in contrast to the hull, the external perimeter and singly connected bonds have non-trivial scaling exponents and logarithmic corrections to scaling.
, contrary to common lore, the hull and perimeter are not the same object.
